Additional comments:

questions.answer: It was easy and straightforward

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: University staff, online sessions and local students

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Since the courses give you only a few credits, it could be quite challenging to get all the courses you want without overlaps

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: choose more courses than the ones you need for the semester. Since the courses give you only a few credits, it could be quite challenging to get all the courses you want without overlaps

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: the courses were shorter than the ones a KU, however the level was very good

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Teaching and evaluation is, in some cases, more learning by hard with less discussion between profesors and students

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Advanced vineyard management; Biology and physiology of the grapevine; Biology and physiology of the grapevine - exercises; Crop production systems in organic agriculture; Ecology and population biology of plants in agro- ecosystems; Field camp I - introduction to mountain forestry and forest sciences; Field course soil ecology; German for Beginners I (A1); Laboratory diagnosis of plant damages; Rhizosphere processes and application to agriculture and soil protection

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend: Ecology and population biology of plants in agro- ecosystems; Biology and physiology of the grapevine and Field camp I - introduction to mountain forestry and forest sciences

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit the vine area. All Austria is beutiful, I think every exchange student should visit Austria first before going to other neighbour countries.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Moderate

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Learn some basics of german. Coming from the extreme Copenhagen is when it comes to danes speaking english, I found myself not being able to communite in english many times.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Language, social behaviours.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: order

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The campus culture, the amazing city of Viena, and the diverse cultures and people one can meet.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Austria is the EU country with the greatest proportion of organic farming, there is a lot to learn about this field.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: the cultural exchange and the learning of new crops and agricultural systems

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language was a challenge, alhtough it did not interfire with my normal life
